title: Why OpenAI Is Secretly Terrified of Open Source AI
angle: OpenAI built its moat on secrecy — but open source just made that moat irrelevant, and insiders know it.

scenes.voiceover: OpenAI has a $90 billion valuation. And they are absolutely terrified of free software.
scenes.visual_description: Bold white text slams onto black screen: '$90 BILLION' then cuts hard to 'TERRIFIED OF... FREE SOFTWARE?' Red pulse effect on cut.
scenes.caption_overlay: Why is the world's most powerful AI company scared of FREE code?

scenes.voiceover: Meta's Llama. Mistral. DeepSeek. All free. All catching up to GPT-4 faster than anyone predicted.
scenes.visual_description: Rapid cuts: GitHub star counts exploding, download bars filling, model benchmark charts with open-source closing the gap on OpenAI scores.
scenes.caption_overlay: Open source models are matching GPT-4... for $0

scenes.voiceover: A leaked Google memo said it directly: 'We have no moat. Neither does OpenAI.' That was 2023. It got worse.
scenes.visual_description: Zoomed-in screen of the leaked Google memo doc, key phrase highlighted in yellow: 'We have no moat.' Camera slowly pushes in. Then hard cut to 2024 benchmark data.
scenes.caption_overlay: "We have no moat. Neither does OpenAI." — leaked Google memo

scenes.voiceover: OpenAI's entire model charges you to use AI. If you can run the same thing locally for free... why would you pay?
scenes.visual_description: Split screen: left side shows OpenAI pricing tiers stacking up in red. Right side shows open-source logos dropping to a giant '$0'. They collide center screen.
scenes.caption_overlay: Their whole business model depends on you NOT knowing this

scenes.voiceover: So they lobbied governments to regulate open source. They called it dangerous. Coincidence? Absolutely not.
scenes.visual_description: Quick cuts: Sam Altman testifying in Senate, news headlines about AI regulation, then slow zoom on OpenAI logo with sinister low-angle lighting.
scenes.caption_overlay: They're trying to use the government to kill the competition

scenes.voiceover: A $90 billion company. Scared of free software. Because when anyone can build what you sell... the game is already over.
scenes.visual_description: Text builds: '$90 BILLION' fades back in from scene 1, then cracks apart pixel by pixel as open-source logos fill the screen. Loop point: last frame mirrors the opening black screen.
scenes.caption_overlay: The $90B company vs. free code. Who wins?

hook_test.viral_proof: Videos using the 'hidden motive behind powerful institution' frame consistently clear 10M+ views. Examples: 'The real reason Apple killed the headphone jack' (14M+), 'Why banks don't want you to know this' (22M+). Conspiracy-adjacent corporate exposure is one of TikTok's highest-retention formats.
hook_test.why_it_works: It fuses financial stakes ($90B), a power imbalance (giant vs. free), and a suppressed truth narrative — triggering algorithmic curiosity loops. Viewers feel smart for watching and angry enough to share.
